  • Sources indicate that few watches make the case for pure design quite as convincingly as the Patek Philippe Golden Ellipse.
  • For 2026 Patek Philippe returns to that formula with the Golden Ellipse (Reference 5738G-001).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Above: Patek Philippe Golden Ellipse watch in white gold, $43,011, patek.com.

Sources indicate that few watches make the case for pure design quite as convincingly as the Patek Philippe Golden Ellipse. Introduced in 1968, its distinctive shape was conceived around the golden ratio, the mathematical proportion found throughout the natural world and long associated with harmony in art and architecture. Neither round nor angular, the curves of the Ellipse have an elemental quality that elevates its simplicity. Despite origins rooted in Renaissance mathematics, the watch also has an unmistakable groovy ’60s elegance.

For 2026 Patek Philippe returns to that formula with the Golden Ellipse (Reference 5738G-001). A larger case gives the watch more presence on the wrist, and at just a hair under 6mm thick, it retains the sleek profile that has always been central to its appeal. Inside is Patek’s ultra-thin self-winding caliber 240, equipped with a 22K gold mini-rotor.

The Golden Ellipse’s ode to nature continues through its use of color. The olive-green sunburst dial—and coordinating calfskin strap—recalls a shade found almost everywhere in the landscape, from leaves and moss to deep forest tones, shifting from an earthy green to brighter grassy flashes as it catches the light. Against the cool white gold case, matching baton markers and slender cheveux-type hands keep the dial remarkably clean.

Nearly six decades after its debut, the Golden Ellipse remains a design classic: mathematics, nature, color, and restraint distilled in one resonant shape.

This story originally appeared in the November 2026 concern of ELLE Decor.

Industry observers note that in October 2024, The Hunting Wives actress Brittany Snow was seen with a mystery man in New York City. He was identified as cinematographer Hunter Moreno, and the pair looked very cozy, sharing a kiss while walking Snow’s dog. The actress was wearing a Yankees cap, a long black coat, wide-leg pants, and a pair of sunglasses for the outing. Moreno was in a baseball cap, jeans, and a major white hoodie.

A year earlier, Snow divorced ex-husband Tyler Stanaland, known for his role on Selling the OC, a spinoff of the popular Netflix reality show, Selling Sunset.

Sources indicate that the former couple declared their split in September 2022 in a joint statement on Instagram that is now deleted, saying, “This decision was made with love and mutual respect for one another. We have realized we need to take some time and make sure we are each living our most fulfilling and authentic lives. We started this journey as best friends and our relationship will continue to be a priority not only for us but for our dog Charlie.”.

It has been revealed that fast-forward to November 2025: reports surfaced that Snow and Moreno had gotten engaged. Snow has since posted tributes to him on Instagram, though she rarely discusses their relationship status herself. A year later, she finally confirmed their engagement.

Here’s what there is to know about Moreno and his relationship with Snow so far.

Moreno is a creative director, cinematographer, and photographer who has worked with celebrities like Selena Gomez, Cara Delevingne, Reneé Rapp, Machine Gun Kelly, Miley Cyrus, and brands like Vogue, Inkd Magazine, and Madewell. He started his career in Los Angeles, filming YouTube videos for growing influencers.

He seems to have been working on directing more music videos in 2024 and was nominated for a directing award at the People’s Choice Country Awards.

He also briefly dated Tana Mongeau in 2017.

Sources indicate that moreno is the co-founder and creative director of Make Sure Your Friends Are OK, or MSYFAO. The organization sells merchandise and then donates a portion of the profits to mental health charities. In an episode of Recovering From Reality with Alexis Haines, he notes he was inspired by his own struggles with mental health issues.

Mental health is an important problem to Snow as well; she co-wrote a book titled September Letters about concerns around mental well-being, partnering with the Mental Health Coalition.

Recent findings suggest that in January 2025, Snow tagged Moreno in a series of photos taken of her for a Netflix press event, crediting him for photographing her. She wrote, “I was asked to hang out a little bit with my friends at @nightagentnetflix. I got to be an agent and run around the streets of Bangkok. Weirdly, I did not wear this dress. 🤍* press for season 2 *”.

Sources indicate that as of July 2025, the two still follow each other on Instagram, and Moreno has liked almost all her recent Instagrams. She also regularly likes his posts.

It has been revealed that yes. On March 28, 2026, Snow quietly tucked a photo of herself with Moreno into an Instagram carousel:.

She shared a birthday tribute to him on Oct. 20, 2026. “Happy birthday to my favorite person on the planet,” she wrote. “I must have done something right to deserve someone like you. Everyone who knows you, knows you are sunshine in human form. This was the first picture we ever took together (we didn’t know it was being taken) and I’ve never stopped hugging you & laughing with you since. It’s my favorite place to be. I love u @huntermoreno.”.

During her November 2026 appearance on Armchair Expert with Dax Shepard, Snow touched on her relationship with Moreno when discussing why she is thankful for her divorce from Tyler Stanaland. “I am so grateful that I went through that because the person that I am and the partner I’m with now, it’s just so different,” she said. “I can’t believe I’m grateful for my divorce. I was 37 and I was living in an Airbnb, just staring at my dog being like, ‘I don’t know what’s going to happen. It’s just you and me, kiddo, and we’re going to try to rebuild this.’”.

Industry observers note that “And I really appreciated so many women, friends of mine that were like, ‘That happened to me,’” she added. “And, you know, I would go on Reddit and look up stories from women going through things in their later 30s and finding people later in life. We have to make it what we make of it.”.

In a recent development, on Nov. 10, 2025, a video surfaced on social media of Snow and Claire Danes talking on the red carpet of The Beast in Me’s premiere. At one point, Danes smiled and asked Snow, “You’re engaged? When did that happen?”.

One day later, TMZ reported that Moreno did indeed pop the question, though Snow has not discussed their status herself.

In a recent development, A year later, on Nov. 19, 2026, Snow finally confirmed the news on The Drew Barrymore Show. When Barrymore asked her about the news, Snow responded, per People, “You know what? For the first time, I’m gonna tell you, I’m gonna tell you. Yes, we’re engaged, yeah,” Snow noted. “I haven’t said it before. It’s okay. It’s not that big of a secret. I mean, like, who cares?”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Alfred Hitchcock put it: “The better the villain, the better the picture.” And nowhere is this truer than for James Bond—a character whose movie is only as good as its baddie.

It has been revealed that jaws, Blofeld, Le Chiffre, Goldfinger—they are the daddies of all baddies; they put the “fun” in funeral, the “ooh-er” in evildoer. They all have a thing, too, because a good baddie always needs a thing. Jaws has the teeth, Le Chiffre the bleeding eye, Blofeld the needy cat, and Goldfinger, well, he’s a kinky old bastard who paints women head to toe in gold to feel like he’s bonking his own bullion.

Which brings me to the question tugging at every Bond fan’s cufflink. Now that Robert Pattinson has been confirmed as the new 007, he’ll need a gold-plated villain to go about “expecting” him.

In a recent development, so which actors would you like to see as the next Bond villain? We have some ideas.

Sources indicate that there was something in the way he played Pennywise in the adaptation of Stephen King’s It that crawled under my skin like a hookworm. I think it’s the eyes. Bill Skarsgård has a mild lazy eye, which he uses in certain roles to create a disorienting swivel-eyed gaze. He used it for Pennywise. He’s a uniquely physical actor, too, well versed in roles that make children cry. He uses his body like a prop, twisting, deforming, looming, leering as the part demands. He played Count Orlok in Nosferatu, Eric Draven in The Crow and Marquis Vincent Bisset de Gramont in John Wick: Chapter 4. A small snag: he recently mentioned he was “spent” playing bad guys. But he added that, if the right Bond villain landed on his desk, he’d be tempted out of baddie retirement for one last job. “[I] just want to go in and do one Mads Mikkelsen villain,” said the actor, referencing Mikkelsen’s character, Le Chiffre, in Casino Royale.

Sources indicate that it’s time for a female lead villain. Sure, Bond has known plenty of miscreant women and seductresses, from Xenia Onatopp (GoldenEye) to Pussy Galore (Goldfinger). But few outright lead villains—hat tip to Lotte Lenya (Rosa Klebb in From Russia with Love) and Sophie Marceau (Elektra King in The World Is Not Enough). It’s a part for a proper actor, a doyenne of screen and stage. A dame, no less. Judi Dench played M across seven films as the one person Bond couldn’t charm, scold, or seduce his way past. Imagine that same withering, headmistress-like authority pointed the other way. Helen Mirren has the gravitas and the twinkle. She’s an Oscar winner who has played a queen, a gangster’s mum in the Fast & Furious films and, of course, the foul-mouthed matriarch Maeve Harrigan in MobLand. She would hardly break a sweat as a Bond villain.

Recent findings suggest that look at that face: the heavy brow, the gaunt cheeks, the dark, brooding eyes. It’s a face that looks like it was carved by candlelight—a mug made for lurking in the shadows. He’s got a bunch of baddies in his locker, from M. Bison in Street Fighter (2026) to Gareth, the Gemini Killer, in Dexter: Resurrection (2025). But perhaps his biggest ace in the hole is his turn as Piter De Vries in Denis Villeneuve’s Dune (2021). Villeneuve likes to work with actors he knows.

Oh, and the other thing: he really wants it. Dastmalchian explained why in a 2023 interview with /Film: “Trust me when I say that I can bring something to an enemy of 007, whether he or she or they be played in a way that no one has ever seen Bond brought to life before, which is, of course, the way that you guys always do it. I think there’s no one to push Bond to the limits of their capabilities the way that I could, and I would love to do it. So there’s my pitch to them. I can’t wait for them to read this.”.

She’s already won an Oscar for playing a corporate villain in Michael Clayton, and she’s never met a prosthetic nose, fur collar or killer blow-dry she couldn’t weaponize... see Snowpiercer’s Minister Mason, Okja’s Lucy Mirando or the White Witch of Narnia—tick, tick, tick. She’s a chameleon with a stare that could freeze a martini.

More than that, Swinton is a master (mistress?) of the in-between, able to embrace and blur lines of gender, age, and species at the click of a slender finger. She possesses that rarest of powers: to change her physical presence, voice, and demeanor so completely as to render herself unrecognizable. Give her a lair, great hair and a long cigarette holder (maybe a Strawberry Ice vape—it’s 2026), and you have a thing of beauty and terror. Because if every great Bond villain needs a thing, Swinton’s is that she can be anything.

#89138. Pink Hair Is Back and Everyone From SZA to Adéla Are Making a Case for It

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (918 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cosmopolitan ↗ Open Full Page

Pink Hair Is Back and Everyone From SZA to Adéla Are Making a Case for It

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (918 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that remember when Kylie Jenner was changing her hair color about every other week, Tumblr was overflowing with pastel-haired girlies, and we were all contemplating whether we could pull off pink hair?
  • From electric pink to soft rose gold, I promise there’s a rosy hue for you.
  • According to recent reports, short answer: Yes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that remember when Kylie Jenner was changing her hair color about every other week, Tumblr was overflowing with pastel-haired girlies, and we were all contemplating whether we could pull off pink hair? Well, dust off your 2016 Pinterest boards, bb, because pink hair is officially making a comeback. But this time, it’s not just King Kylie leading the charge. SZA, Adéla, and even Martha Stewart have been putting their own spins on the color, proving that there’s no one way (or age!) to enter your pink hair era. “Since pink is not a natural hair color, you don’t really have to abide by any typical color analysis rules,” notes colorist Emily Claire, which means you have free range to do whatever the heck you’d like.

And the range is range-ing. From electric pink to soft rose gold, I promise there’s a rosy hue for you. Personally, I’m loving this return to hair color that’s just fun—and I’m not the only one. “Recently my clients with pink hair have been requesting baby pink and deep berry pink,” notes colorist Cara Craig. Plus, Cosmo called out pink as a top fall hair color trend this year. So, whether you’re ready to go full-on Barbie or want to experiment with a subtle rosy tint, there’s a pink hair idea with your name on it. Ahead, we’re breaking it all down, including how to choose your shade, what to ask for at the salon, and how to keep your pink hair looking fresh.

According to recent reports, short answer: Yes. There’s a truly pink hair color for everyone. “I have clients asking for all shades of pink, from blush and rose gold to hot pink to magenta,” notes hairstylist Alyssa Chapa.

According to recent reports, pink is surprisingly so versatile, so there are plenty of ways to make it work for you. “In my opinion, pink is a neutral. I think of fashion colors as cousins to classic shades,” states Craig. “So if you are a blonde, consider baby pink. If you are a brunette you’ll want to move to darker pinks and fuchsias. If you want to feel like a redhead then wear rose golds and warm pinks.” She also recommends a violet pink if you prefer keeping things cool-toned.

Wondering about how your skin tone will look with pink hair? “I’m personally of the opinion that there is no right or wrong shade for your skin tone,” claims Chapa, but if it’s really important to you, here are her tips for finding the best hair color for your skin tone. “Start by figuring out your undertones,” she says. “I like using the veins on the inside of the wrist; if you have blue or purple veins then you usually have cool undertones, green veins mean warm undertones, and a mixture of both is a neutral undertone.” Then, it’s pretty easy from there: Match your undertones to the shade of pink, which your colorist will be able to help out with (think baby or icy pink for cool tones, peach or salmon pink for warm tones, that kind of thing).

First things first: Bring reference photos to your colorist—we’ve handily included some pics throughout this story for ya. After all, Adéla’s vivid pink and Stewart’s subtle rose gold hair require very different approaches, so you’ll want to make sure you’re specific about what shade you’re after.

“For most people, unless you happen to be naturally blonde, the process would involve lightening your hair to the desired level with bleach, then toning it to the desired pink with a direct dye,” states Claire.

According to recent reports, need some specific pink hair ideas? These are colorist-approved: “One of my favorite ways to wear pink lately is over classic blonde highlights,” says Craig. “I also love a pink double process (e.g. Adéla).” Double process just means a two-step coloring method—your colorist will first bleach/lighten your hair, then apply the pink color. You can also go with chunky highlights, “especially a halo hairline where the pink frames the face,” adds Chapa. “Mixing chunky pink highlights in with shades of red or brown to create a kind of calico effect is also popular online.”.

Now for the not-so-fun part: Pink hair doesn’t necessarily equal low-maintenance hair. “No matter the tone, you’re going to have to refresh it in four to six weeks if you want it to stay pink,” notes Chapa. If you want to go as low-maintenance as possible, a softer pink is the way to go, notes Craig.

For a more natural-looking grow-out or to keep your hair color easy, “your alternatives are to choose an already muted color like a dusty rose or mauve and let it fade to blonde or brunette, or to invest in an at-home color depositing treatment to maintain your pink until your next salon visit,” Chapa says.

You can help extend your color by washing less frequently, using color-safe shampoo and conditioner, limiting heat styling, and incorporating a color-depositing mask or at-home hair gloss. “I always recommend my clients use a pink-tinted shampoo or conditioner to keep up with the color between appointments at home,” says Claire.

Sources indicate that catharine Malzahn is a contributing beauty writer at Cosmo. She’s covered all things skincare, makeup, hair, and more, including trending haircuts and hair colors you have to try.

This St. Bart’s House Was Designed to Look Nothing Like Its Neighbors

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1066 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elledecor

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Few clients ask their designer to make the bedrooms in their vacation home smaller and simpler, but that was just the edit the homeowners made to plans for their house in St.
  • Sources indicate that situated on a steep hillside above one of St.
  • According to recent reports, A Caribbean island is a challenging place to work under any circumstances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Few clients ask their designer to make the bedrooms in their vacation home smaller and simpler, but that was just the edit the homeowners made to plans for their house in St. Bart’s, says designer David Ries. “They didn’t want these humongous bedrooms with huge floating beds and massive bathrooms.” Instead, the couple wanted to be able to host as many people as possible, a request that didn’t surprise Ries, who’d already worked with the family on homes in Manhattan, Long Island, and Telluride. “It’s what this client has always asked for. They can’t have enough bedrooms.”.

Sources indicate that situated on a steep hillside above one of St. Bart’s famously pristine white sand beaches, the house had initially been a boutique hotel. The plan was to turn it into a retreat for themselves and their adult children and grandchildren. The family are longtime visitors to the island—“the daughter told me it was her ‘happy place,’” states Ries, lead designer of the Upcoming York-based interior design firm Ries Hayes—and knew exactly what they wanted. Not the white box look popular with luxury new builds on the island, but instead something reminiscent of the “old St. Bart’s,” says East Hampton-based landscape designer Edwina von Gal, who, like Ries, has collaborated with the clients on other projects.

According to recent reports, A Caribbean island is a challenging place to work under any circumstances. Everything has to be brought in from far away, including all the plants, which came by barge from Miami. St. Bart’s in particular requires anyone building to work with a local architect and engineer. In their initial proposal, this French team defaulted to that “slick and modernist” look, as von Gal describes it, with the oversized bedrooms and white color scheme that dominates much of the island’s luxury housing stock.

The design team pushed back—asking for a lot of bedrooms (eight) and generous living spaces. They also had strong opinions on the building materials. Given the island’s climate, the humid, salt-soaked air can be hard on everything. “If we did white paint, which is prominent throughout St. Bart's, it’s constant maintenance, constant painting,” indicates Ries. The design team insisted on cladding the buildings in Ipe, the durable tropical hardwood, which wears well. It mystified the local architects and set the complex apart from its neighbors. It also makes the buildings disappear into the greenery of the hillside.

But the architects rapidly caught on to the fresh plans, and von Gal is eager to praise their technical accomplishments. Regulations require properties to conserve rainwater, so there are cisterns beneath the buildings, plus technology infrastructure and laundry facilities. “Working on the hill is so complex,” she claims. “It's such a tight little package of technology and function. What they did was amazing.”.

Recent findings suggest that the team decided to reconfigure the property as a series of pavilions that face the view of the ocean and surrounding hills. The main entry is at the top of the steep hill, along with parking. The next level down is for family bedrooms; below that is a primary suite and study; and finally the fourth level is the main living space, including a playroom. “We made sure this playroom was front and center,” notes Ries. “My client loves her grandkids.”.

The playroom and study have built-in daybeds that can be used as spare guest rooms in a pinch. But the clients did get their eight bedrooms. “We know how to make compact bedrooms and make them very efficient, make them very livable, which allows us to fit in a lot of space for a lot of guests, and then that puts a lot of emphasis on having main entertaining spaces that are big and gracious,” notes Ries. “The idea is that everybody hangs out together.”.

Everything is united by generous outdoor spaces, which wind between the bedrooms. “Every room has an amazing view,” states Ries. “It feels almost like your own little treehouse in a way.” The bottom living area opens out to a pool and an expansive deck where the family eats most of their meals.

The house has an elevator, but stairs are the primary way the family moves between levels and finally down to the beach. “We hung on for a really great, gracious, fun set of stairs,” says von Gal. “They really introduce you to how amazing the different levels are and all the wonderful secret places.”.

Durable fabrics and materials were chosen throughout and Ries made sure everything could be easily moved around and reconfigured. Outside on the main deck, three long dining tables from Sutherland were outfitted with casters so they could be maneuvered into a single long table or several smaller ones; 26 lightweight dining chairs can be pulled from different parts of the deck. If the infamous “Christmas winds” bring a downpour, the tables can even be moved indoors so a dinner party can proceed in inclement weather. Outdoor seating can be arranged as a 15-foot sofa or several love seats.

Sources indicate that “It's so flexible,” notes Ries. “We know this from working with a client that their needs for entertaining change every day, or sometimes a couple times a day.”.

Recent findings suggest that the kitchen is also efficient, designed to produce easy, clean meals. The family would rather spend time in the pool than over a stove. And no part of the living room is oriented around a TV. “They're readers,” claims Ries. “There’s always stacks of newly introduced books when you go to their homes. So there’s all these cool little spots you can tuck into.”.

It has been revealed that ultimately, the client and design team’s insistence on what they wanted paid off—but it wasn’t without a few moments of doubt. “When so many people are telling you ‘no, surely this is not what you want,’ it does start to erode your confidence a little,” says von Gal. “Then when it does come out well, there’s a real sense of triumph and satisfaction.”.

#89136. This Wood Finish Was Once Seen as “Outdated.” But Designers Now Say It's Coming Back.

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1077 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housebeautiful ↗ Open Full Page

This Wood Finish Was Once Seen as “Outdated.” But Designers Now Say It's Coming Back.

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1077 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, for a period of time in the late 1980s to early 2000s, it seemed virtually impossible to enter a house and not come across honey oak.
  • “You’d see it everywhere—cabinetry, trim, stair railings, and floors.
  • Recent findings suggest that however, there’s been a noticeable shift in the way people are wanting their interiors to look, and warmer spaces are definitely back in style.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, for a period of time in the late 1980s to early 2000s, it seemed virtually impossible to enter a house and not come across honey oak. That bright, orange-toned wood finish covered kitchen cabinets, bathroom vanities, even baseboard trim and furniture around the house.

“You’d see it everywhere—cabinetry, trim, stair railings, and floors. It was the go-to wood tone for builders and homeowners alike,” Cathleen Gruver of Gruver Cooley tells House Beautiful. “But by the early 2000s, it started to fall out of favor as people shifted toward cooler, more neutral interiors.”.

Recent findings suggest that however, there’s been a noticeable shift in the way people are wanting their interiors to look, and warmer spaces are definitely back in style. With this evolution, can we expect to see a revival of honey oak, as well? We asked a handful of designers if they think this golden wood finish is back, and how they would style it for modern-day interiors.

Elizabeth Bennett and Mallory Robins, the founders of interior design studio Kobel + Co, believe honey oak is back for two reasons: The first is that warm tones throughout the entirety of the home are on the rise; the second is that honey oak has a lot of nostalgic associations for people who grew up in the '80s and '90s and are now homeowners.

“We're seeing a resurgence of styles from this era not only in homes, but in fashion as well, as we harken back to a pre-digital era,” Bennett explains.

In a recent development, “It’s not necessarily a full-blown comeback, but I’ve definitely noticed a soft return—particularly in cabinetry, millwork details, and furniture," Gruver says. “Clients aren’t always asking for 'honey oak' by name, but they are gravitating toward natural wood tones that offer warmth and character.”.

It has been revealed that before you take a sledgehammer to those original honey oak cabinets, reconsider this tone by styling it in more modern ways. Keep reading to see fresh ways that designers are working with honey oak in their new projects.

Industry observers note that as homeowners gravitate more toward lived-in, inviting interiors, honey oak is a wonderful way to add warmth. Leave it to the professionals to find stylish ways to make this once-outdated wood tone look cool again.

Plenty of designers will tell you to mix wood tones in your home to prevent it from feeling one-note, and the same is encouraged when honey oak makes a major presence. When designer Adina Hall took on the project above, there was too much honey oak in the space for her team to replace or refinish it all, so they embraced it instead.

In a recent development, “We developed a custom stain for the newly introduced wood floors, a whitewashed French oak that created a neutral canvas for the structure without competing with the existing honey tone,” Hall says. “We added custom cabinetry finished in a taupe-tone ash veneer, again a neutral tone, and we leaned into crisp whites and some cool tones like sage green and indigo blue as accents to create a balanced palette.”.

In a recent development, heavy amounts of warm woods can overwhelm the eye; it’s notable to build a restrained palette and introduce interest with cooler tones, wood stains, sculptural furniture, and contrasting materials. “The key is to give the honey oak a contemporary context in order to make it feel like an intentional material that delivers a punch of warmth in an otherwise cool and architecturally bold yet restrained palette.”.

According to recent reports, whether you’re adding in fresh honey oak or you’re trying to work around what’s already in your home, one of the best ways to ensure it feels modern and not like a ‘90s Tuscan-inspired home is choosing an earthy color palette. Muted greens, warm whites, greiges, taupe, light blues—these are all beautiful hues that won’t add even more orange-ish warmth to your space.

Sources indicate that “Instead of making honey oak the focus of the room, I let the beauty of the wood shine through the use of clean lines, black matte touches, natural stones, and modern lighting,” designer Nancy Dow of Sierra Living Concepts says. She’s fond of using this wood, and uses these shades to create a modern and fresh appearance.

Rather than “wood drenching” a home in a single tone (as was often seen in the early aughts), Robins explains that current homeowners are exercising more restraint with their finishes. “Rather than the primary finish for a house on trim, floors, and cabinetry, it's being used in more subtle ways—a cased good piece or a kitchen island alone,” she indicates.

Industry observers note that one of the reasons honey oak fell out of style is because it is a very warm tone, and in the world of “millennial gray,” an orange-tinted kitchen or bathroom isn’t very appealing. However, designer Marli Jones of Rebel House design studio believes this can be fixed simply by creating a contrasting palette.

According to recent reports, in the kitchen space above, Jones used only honey oak cabinetry in the scullery to contrast the light, bright main kitchen. “It adds a coziness to the scullery and envelops the space in warm, natural tones,” she indicates. “That same honey color travels across the countertop stone and into the tile backsplash.” The two rooms are connected by the wall of glass and steel, but the change in materiality from the white cabinets to the honey oak creates a dynamic transition. “Warm wood always adds a grounding layer.”.

When adding a honey oak piece into your home, do so intentionally. Opt for a “stunning built-in, a custom island, or as an accent detail that brings texture and warmth,” Gruver indicates. To emphasize the styling, pair the honey oak piece with contemporary hardware or painted elements to help it feel fresh and curated.

While honey oak can work in any interior aesthetic, there are a few styles it looks best in, according to Gruver: updated farmhouse and cottagecore. Basically, “any space that leans into character, craft, and comfort,” she explains. However, she's also seen the tone used successfully in more modern, organic spaces where there's a large emphasis on natural materials and textures. It all depends on how it's balanced, which holds true for any wood tone. She adds, “When styled right, honey oak can absolutely feel current again.”.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that “The hardest part was having something as intimate and personal as a diary become public,” notes Plestia Alaqad of her decision to publish her diary-memoir, The Eyes of Gaza.
  • Alaqad’s reporting situated herself as a voice for the ordinary.
  • Industry observers note that alaqad left Gaza for Lebanon, where she is completing her master’s degree.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that “The hardest part was having something as intimate and personal as a diary become public,” notes Plestia Alaqad of her decision to publish her diary-memoir, The Eyes of Gaza. The book details the harrowing first weeks after October 7 in Gaza as a young Palestinian journalist. Alaqad studied new media and journalism at Eastern Mediterranean University in Cyprus before returning to her home in 2022. Intending to educate the world about her city, she did not know she would end up reporting the first stages of the genocide.

Alaqad’s reporting situated herself as a voice for the ordinary. In the first few days, she spoke to her neighbors and local children. Her reporting appeared mostly on her Instagram account, which grew to a little over 2 million followers, with many of her images republished by the BBC, The New York Times, PBS NewsHour, and The Washington Post. Even through the chaos and the expulsion of over 100,000 Gazans in the first few days, according to UNHCR, which Alaqad also recounts in her memoir, there are moments of tenderness caught by her and everyday Gazans she would meet and talk to. Her style of reporting is grounded in a sense of familiarity, narrating the everyday in extraordinary circumstances. She made connections with people in a way that makes you feel like you were alongside her, drinking tea with the local tetas and jiddos, watching the violence and the world collapse around you.

Industry observers note that alaqad left Gaza for Lebanon, where she is completing her master’s degree. During the course of our interview, she spoke openly with me about the loneliness of the isolation of being a witness, forever changed by the devastation.

One of my favorite things about Gaza is the people and the sense of community. For example, the relationship between my neighbors and I. I’ve been living in the Al -Waleed Building since I was almost four years old, and I know all my neighbors. Like Dana, who lived next door next to me—it was like having a sister and best friend nearby at all times. Whenever I needed anything, I just knocked at Dana’s door. If I needed help picking out an outfit, if I needed help replying to messages, even if I was just bored and I wanted someone to hang out with, it was always Dana who I turned to. There’s something about Gaza that just is home to me. There is simplicity and a love for life in Gaza that I haven’t seen elsewhere in the world. So being born and raised there always meant having loving and supportive people around me.

According to recent reports, there’s more to us than being occupied. We’re full of talent and art we never got the time to make, because we’re too busy worrying if the people we love will still be alive tomorrow. That’s what pushes me to keep writing.

I’m interested in writing and telling stories of people. I recently interviewed Renad Atallah and wrote a piece about her for The New Arab. Also, one of my favorite pieces I wrote was an interview with Alaa Abu Diab, a one-of-a-kind comedian, for The National.

Recent findings suggest that as of recently, I started my newsletter on Substack, where I share a personal essay every week on Gaza, girlhood, friendship, and everything in between. My ultimate hope would be to tell stories about a free Palestine one day. And as a journalist, I’ll always see my work as incomplete without going back to Gaza and continuing to tell Palestinian stories from the ground. And hopefully work on an international level and tell stories of people who suffered because of war and conflicts in other countries.

Recent findings suggest that I enjoy reading nonfiction books and memoirs because I love learning about people and their experiences. I remember reading Anne Frank’s diary in middle school.… I remember how it made me feel and the impact it had on me.

I have also always been drawn to personal writings, like Franz Kafka’s letters and the letters between Ghassan Kanafani and Ghada al-Samman. I think I’m a very curious person by nature, and I’m interested in understanding what is happening in people’s minds, and if I get the chance to read strangers’ diaries, I wouldn't say no. That curiosity is something that inspired me.

Growing up, I always had a diary. It was me and my purple diary against the world.… For me, journaling has always been my safe space in the world. It’s the one place where I can write whatever I want without feeling judged. That’s honestly why I wanted to create Neya [Alaqad’s creative brand], which is an Arabic word that means intention. The first product will be a journal, of course, and it will come in four different colors. Each journal has a small, kind reminder on the hardcover and little sweet quotes throughout the pages because I wanted to create something that is personal and safe, something you would want to come back to and share your thoughts in. For me, journaling has always been where I can reconnect with myself. I hope Neya can become that for other people too: a small space where they can pause, reflect, and reconnect with themselves.

It has been revealed that the hardest part was having something as intimate and personal as a diary become public. Something that was once only mine suddenly was in the hands of people from all around the world. I always try to think about the impact it could have on others, and I’m grateful that this time we get to tell our own stories rather than having our stories told on our behalf. I’m also grateful for the readers around the world who have read The Eyes of Gaza and are making the effort to educate themselves about Palestine.

According to recent reports, I often feel like I am living in two worlds. On one hand, I have the opportunity to do things that many people back home cannot access freely, such as pursuing my education and continuing my master’s degree. On the other hand, I carry the weight of knowing what is happening to my people and my land, without having any superpower to stop it.

I always try to stay honest and true to myself, and I try to take people through this journey with me online. I share the contradictions, the pain, and the moments of hope. What it’s like trying to process the experience of having your homeland bombed, your city erased, and your people murdered, while also surviving and trying to make sense of the world outside. It is something that is difficult to put into words.

Recent findings suggest that it feels like time has frozen in Gaza, while the rest of the world continues moving forward. And for those of us away from home, we are constantly trying to live between these two realities.

Sources indicate that gaza is a place where contradictions exist side by side. You see unimaginable grief, but you also see people trying to find meaning and strength in the middle of that suffering.

Sources indicate that the Eyes of Gaza captures these contradictions. On one page, sadness may take over, while on another, hope emerges. Ultimately, I believe that when people experience powerful emotions, they are often moved to take action.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Parker Selman and Karan Rai’s love story was born from a sunset. “Our paths crossed a few times before, but the first time we remember speaking was on a roof as we watched the sun go down our senior year at Tufts University,” Parker recalls. A few weeks later, they found themselves alone on a dance floor. “I looked down at my phone to see it was midnight and, therefore, officially my birthday,” Parker says. “I told him he should give me a kiss because it was my birthday, and he did. We were both smitten, and constantly in one another's orbit.” Despite the two lining up jobs on opposite coasts, they swiftly realized being practical was not an option, and Karan managed to convince his company to transfer him to New York.

According to recent reports, the couple got engaged on a crisp autumn walk around Governors Island—Parker’s favorite spot in the city. She owns and operates a wedding photography business, and as they strolled along, she asked to take a picture of Karan on her medium-format camera with their apartment building and skyline in the background. “While I was snapping the photo, he got down on one knee,” she says, “and I had the privilege of capturing my own proposal.” They rode the ferry back to Manhattan and went to Della’s, a local wine bar, where their families and friends were waiting to celebrate.

Two months later, she proposed back. “While we were walking in Sun Valley, I requested he take a picture of me sitting in the snow with our dog Grumpy,” she states. "I proposed the same way he proposed to me, the moment captured on my Rolleiflex.” Parker used diamonds and emeralds from her late great-grandmother’s engagement ring and gold from Karan’s late grandmother’s earrings to create his signet ring.

In a recent development, their multi-day wedding unfolded in early September 2026 near Sun Valley, Idaho (where Parker’s family lives). They chose Central Idaho 4-H Camp, located 30 minutes outside of town, for its series of cabins and a large field up in the mountains. “The space was a blank canvas with no sound ordinance,” she notes. “Studio Sully transformed the campsite into something magical.”.

In a recent development, going into the planning process, the couple knew they wanted the entire event to feel like a fusion of their cultures. In the days leading up to the Sun Valley celebration, Karan’s parents threw a series of traditional Indian wedding ceremonies and celebrations in his hometown of Pleasanton, California. Once guests arrived in Idaho, they all checked in at The Sun Valley Lodge, where each day the couple had organized group activities.

Festivities kicked off on Friday with a Western-themed welcome party at their favorite après-ski bar, Grumpy’s. Parker wore a tweed corset and skirt by Wiederhoeft accessorized with brown leather Manolo Blahniks and a wooden horse purse by Vin. When the weather cooled down, she tossed on a vintage suede fringe RRL jacket. Karan followed a similar script and wore a Bode suede fringe jacket and One of These Days pants with a painted horse and cowboy detail on the knees. His bandana was made by his mother. “She created a piece inspired by Marie Lichtenberg’s jeweled bandana, utilizing earrings and jewelry of Karan’s grandmothers, mother, and sister,” Parker indicates.

Sources indicate that guests were encouraged to wear textiles, paisley, and eclectic patterns to evoke a Wild West meets India atmosphere. In one corner, Boise Thread Studio set up shop to embroider initials onto trucker hats, shirts, and bandanas. Meanwhile, guests drank schooners (the name for Grumpy’s beer chalices) on the patio and ate burgers and hot dogs. “Karan and I named our beloved miniature dachshund Grumpy after the bar’s corn dogs, so it is only fitting that we ordered them until they ran out,” Parker claims. Her mother welcomed the group with a sunset toast before moving inside. “We took over the electronic jukebox and closed down the restaurant until Karan had to stand up on the booth to usher everyone out the door.”.

In a recent development, the next afternoon they hosted a sangeet by the Massive Wood River. “The estate has a series of winding paths that lead to the riverside, and we wanted the afternoon portion to feel like a mountain garden party with activities and upcoming discoveries tucked into each corner,” Parker notes. The flowing river and live music by Boise-based Ashley Rose Band served as the soundtrack as guests played croquet, horseshoes, and badminton. Near the band, Henna by Sanjana created patterns on guests' hands.

Parker wore Danielle Frankel’s cream Mariela dress featuring two layers of hand-painted wildflowers. “I wanted a long braid with flowers woven in, and Jasmine Burnside helped bring the vision to life,” she indicates. Karan wore a light blue Jatin Malik sherwani with juttis from his personal collection.

As the sun set, guests were escorted to a clearing where a buffet was set up for dinner, and the dance floor was built around a large willow tree. The vignette was inspired by a 1905 Impressionist painting called Nighttime Festivities that depicts a turn-of-the-century party beneath the trees of a French palace. “I told Melissa [Sully] I wanted the sangeet to be based on this and we became obsessed with bringing the painting to life,” Parker explains. Lights and flowers were strung into the branches that draped overhead. Karan’s parents and Parker’s best friend, Ana, gave speeches before a series of traditional dances were performed by various family members and friends, followed by a lively dance floor courtesy of DJ Anupya.

The morning of the wedding, Parker and Karan got ready with their families and friends. “We are terrible at surprises, and he had seen my dress many times before, so I saw no purpose in a first look,” she notes. The couple set off in a convertible (Parker’s hair protected in a vintage scarf from the year she was born), stopping at a vista for photos before arriving at the venue.

It has been revealed that for her wedding look, Parker worked with Patricia Voto of One/Of to create a custom gown inspired by Christian Dior’s 1955 Soirée de Lahore. Early on, she knew she wanted something that felt like a combination of Karan and herself. “The original gown was made by the designer two years before his death and was based on a sari with the one-shoulder design and gold embroidery,” she explains. All of the embroidery was done in India, and Parker paired the gown with a custom One/Of veil featuring gold embroidery along the edge, as well as light green shoes by Paula Nadal.

Sources indicate that karan wore a custom Bode tuxedo with a golden sunflower detail, and as a boutonniere, he wore his own emerald kalgi (a traditional Indian headpiece for turbans). “His cufflinks and studs were my late grandfather’s, his cummerbund was unbranded vintage ’70s made in India with embellished sunflowers, and his shoes were suede Hermès.”.

Industry observers note that guests arrived to the ceremony dressed in jewel tones and metallics, walking down a pathway with giant sunflowers on either side. Parker and her mother, an amateur florist, had collaborated with Madison of Hart Floral to create the dramatic entrance. “When I spoke of our love for sunflowers and our desire to have them serve as a recurring visual throughout the day, Madison and Melissa joined forces,” Parker explains.

Sources indicate that for the ceremony, they stood within a chuppah structure with draped gold chainmail and burgundy sunflower motifs. Karan’s best friend Drew officiated the ceremony, and the fathers of her late friends Alex and Josh read an excerpt by Ovid of the Greek myth of Baucis and Philemon. “Karan’s vows and my own were mirrors of each other. Unknowingly, we made many of the same references, and we each ended by quoting the story of Baucis and Philemon, who, when they died, received the honor of becoming intertwined as trees so they could live on forever.”.

Coming from mixed religious backgrounds (Karan’s parents are Sikh and Hindu and Parker’s are Episcopalian and Jewish), the couple chose to honor both. “Karan arrived on horseback as a nod to traditional Punjabi weddings. St. Christopher medallions were placed on each program, and my sister, Alison, shared a short speech about the patron saint of travelers, the namesake of the church we attended as children, and spoke about the new journey Karan and I were embarking upon,” Parker says. “My sister-in-law, Kareena, shared a speech about the jaimala ceremony as a nod to the Hindu wedding tradition, and spoke about the importance of seeing each other as equals.” Karan’s maternal uncle led the group in a Sikh Ardas prayer, and the ceremony ended with the Jewish tradition of the breaking of the glass. As the couple exited, guests threw dried bougainvillea from Karan’s family garden in Chandigarh.

Cocktail hour kicked off with oysters shipped from Island Creek Oyster Co. (the site of the couple’s first two dates). “We really wanted textiles to be an important decor motif throughout the celebration,” Parker claims, noting that there was leveled seating overlaid with rugs, a rug-covered bar, and a rug-covered makeshift bandstand. Later on, their sisters shared speeches, and the couple danced to “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You,” then launching into “Dancing in the Moonlight” as tambourines were passed to guests. “Guests followed Karan and I through the field to reveal the tent, set among the cabins.”.

Recent findings suggest that the band continued to play as guests entered the tent and danced. At each seat, Parker and Karan placed a letter explaining what their friendship meant to the couple. After the buzz died down, Parker’s father opened the evening with a speech. “We then had a family-style dinner of our favorite bites: kale salad, focaccia, Idaho trout, pesto gnocchi, and vodka meatballs,” she claims.

Recent findings suggest that after dinner wrapped up, Parker and her father danced to “Wide Open Spaces” (a song they listened to as she was growing up) before everyone joined in. The couple snuck away to cut the cake—a 30-inch round flourless chocolate confection covered in raspberries—which was passed out on the outskirts of the dance floor. Indian sweets called ladoos were also passed around.

After a full week of wedding events between California for the traditional Indian celebration and four days in Sun Valley, the two were understandably exhausted. “It took weeks to recover, but the whole time all we could talk about was how deeply happy we were.”.

If you’re looking to elevate your kitchen, take a cue from our Whole Home. This design is bold enough to impress the design-obsessed and practical enough for the bustle of everyday life.

Sources indicate that the Traitors may be a game of deceit, but Victor Vollbrechthausen and Katie Fites’ flirtation? That was apparently very real.

As the first civilian-only season of The Traitors: Upcoming Blood came to a close, host Alan Cumming asked Katie, “Is there a possible date on the cards for you and Victor?”.

Sources indicate that she seemed tainted by the fact that Victor had banished her, jokingly saying, “No date for you,” until he kept the banter going and claimed that he “earned it” after finding out she was a Traitor. Now, the star-crossed Faithful and Traitor romance has seemingly made its way out of Alan’s Scottish castle.

During a joint postseason interview with Entertainment Weekly, Victor and Katie revealed they followed through on their intends and actually went on a first date.

Recent findings suggest that “We have gone on that date. After incessant begging, let the kids back home know that persistence works,” Katie joked, before revealing that it was “great.”.

According to recent reports, “It was fun to get to know each other outside of her trying to murder me, me trying not to get murdered. It was nice to take a moment just for us,” Victor, who played as a Faithful while Katie was one of the season’s Traitors, told the outlet.

Industry observers note that as for what their first date entailed? Well, there was certainly no discussion about their time on the show, since Victor banned any mention of it. And, honestly, who can blame him? After all, he was onto Katie’s strategy to potentially target him for murder.

Recent findings suggest that while her crush on Victor helped her game, Katie admitted that she genuinely enjoyed hanging out with him and even grew close to him throughout the season. She also revealed that she didn’t immediately kill Victor off because she wasn’t aware of his suspicions toward her—though he had been side-eyeing her earlier on than she realized.

The pair remained coy about whether they’ll keep their showmance going offscreen. When asked if they had aims to go on a second date, Victor shared, “Let’s see. Listen, man, it’s gonna... I don’t know. Getting that first one was an uphill battle, but I think there could be.”.

“I think there could be,” Katie added. “But we’ll see. Gonna have to keep persisting.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’re reading this, there’s probably a holiday gift exchange on your calendar coming up. Maybe your boss organized one for the office, or maybe it’s the doing of that one friend who loves hosting so much they’d throw a party for Arbor Day. Either way, you’re probably wondering: What the heck do I bring to this thing?

According to recent reports, there are a few rules to this game. First, there’s likely a price cap, so we’re keeping everything under $100. (If your white elephant involves luxury gifts, we’d love to be a fly on that very well-appointed wall.) Second, your gift should be something just about anyone would be excited to unwrap. That rules out clothes and shoes with specific sizes, phone cases for whatever iPhone model is at the moment in circulation, and franchise merch that assumes your giftee has seen every Marvel movie or follows football.

Recent findings suggest that luckily, that still leaves plenty of fun, affordable, crowd-pleasing gifts. We’ve rounded up our favorites below, so pick one, wrap it up, and take all the credit when everyone starts fighting over it.

Who doesn’t like waffles? A waffle-maker that’s easy to use and easy to store is for sure going to be a slam dunk at the gift exchange.

Sources indicate that A cute felt ornament is a great gift that’s sort of holiday-themed, but also makes a fun gift for any occasion. It will take their Christmas tree to the next level—and even if they don’t celebrate Christmas, they can hang this little guy on a doorknob, at their desk, etc.

According to recent reports, jigsaw puzzles have always been a popular pastime, but people (ahem, my mom and sister) have especially taken up puzzling since the pandemic. Piecework makes some of my favorite puzzles, like this quirky peppermint-themed one.

Sources indicate that whether they drink coffee or tea, this leakproof tumbler will no doubt become their go-to drink vessel. Coffee for the morning commute? Check. Hot tea for an afternoon pick-me-up? Check. A glass of wine with dinner? Sure, why not. The Strova has all that covered (literally).

In these cold-weather months, hand cream is a must. This luxurious one from Homecourt smells like cedarwood smoke, sweet cardamom, cinnamon, and white leather.

According to recent reports, everyone wants a home that smells good. Aera’s aroma diffuser will make that happen. Yes, it’s at the upper limit price-wise, but it’s bound to be the gift everyone wants.

Just any old liquor won’t cut it, but Fords Sloe Gin is perfect for the holidays. Whoever gets this bottle will be making Sloe Gin Fizzes all winter long, and if you’re lucky, they’ll invite you over for one.

This rechargeable candle lighter is both practical and artful—it eliminates the need for matches altogether, and it looks classy next to a candle.

Yes, a candle is a classic gift exchange option, but don’t just go for your run-of-the-mill Yankee Candle; get one that will make their home smell like a winter wonderland.

Sources indicate that who wouldn’t want a tiny printer that can instantly print photos from your phone? This one comes with a paper roll so your giftee can get started printing as soon as they open this awesome present.

Everyone needs a hat in the winter, so why not make it a nice cashmere beanie from Quince? They won’t know you only spent $35 on it—that’s how luxurious it feels.

In a recent development, this set of extra virgin olive oil and balsamic vinegar from Kosterina is a great gift for anyone who cooks, whether they’re a beginner or a professional chef. And the fun holiday packaging is a plus!

Industry observers note that another thing everyone needs? A toiletry bag. No matter where they’re going this holiday season, they’ll need a place to pack their toothbrush, comb, razor, and whatever other bathroom essentials they use. Why not pack them in this cute pouch from Brooklinen?

Sources indicate that everyone is getting into peptides now. Make it easy for whoever gets this gift to start their peptide journey with this duo from Naturium.

It has been revealed that gloves don’t have to be boring. Verloop makes fun, colorful pairs that, yes, are touchscreen compatible. Everyone will want to get their hands on (and in) these.

A tiny record player that can actually play (tiny) records? It’s the dream of any music lover who lives in a small apartment!

Help someone get organized with a fun planner they’ll actually want to use. Burga has tons of cool patterns, so choose one you think will appeal to most people.

Industry observers note that A tote bag is the versatile catch-all bag everyone should have at least one of. And these mini ones from Steele are so cute and will last forever.

In a recent development, if you’re going to go with a food gift, make it a Classic Panettone holiday cake from Eataly. Everyone will want a piece of this.

According to recent reports, pretty much anything from the MoMA Design Store is guaranteed to be a hit, and it will probably be the most unique gift at the party. Take these colorful crystal glasses, for example. Who wouldn’t want these in their kitchen?

#89125. What to Eat for Healthier Skin and Slower Aging

What to Eat for Healthier Skin and Slower Aging

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2110 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor.
  • Industry observers note that on the quest to age smarter and slower, there’s a lot that your skin care can do.
  • To understand the connection between diet and skin health, Caitlin Hosmer, MS, RD, LDN, a registered dietitian and co-founder of MenoPantry, notes it’s important to define the notion of slowing down aging.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Industry observers note that on the quest to age smarter and slower, there’s a lot that your skin care can do. But perhaps one of the greatest contributions lies in the foods you consistently eat. Of course, diet and exercise are the pillars of good health, proper body function, and longevity, but a recent study done by scientists at the German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE) also reveals that 10 specific diets are linked to slower aging. Experts unpack the findings for ELLE and break down which foods you should incorporate or ditch from your diet to help improve skin health.

To understand the connection between diet and skin health, Caitlin Hosmer, MS, RD, LDN, a registered dietitian and co-founder of MenoPantry, notes it’s important to define the notion of slowing down aging. She points out that this particular DZNE study didn’t look at wrinkles or how old people feel. “It looked at biological aging, measured with epigenetic clocks. These read chemical marks on our DNA (methylation) that shift as our cells age. In about 7,500 adults, the researchers found that following any of 10 healthy eating patterns more closely was associated with slower biological aging,” Hosmer explains. The 10 eating patterns or diets included in the study results are Mediterranean, Nordic, DASH, MIND, and plant-based. Hosmer says that while the effect was modest, this kind of study highlights an association, not causation—proof that diet is the reason for the positive outcome—so it is still a meaningful signal.

Sources indicate that additionally, Mark Gilbert, nutritionist from The 1:1 Diet by Cambridge Weight Strategy, tells ELLE that no single food has been satisfactorily studied and shown to be likely, on its own, to slow aging. “Of all the predictors of a long, healthy life, two of the best, which can be improved with diet, are muscle mass and strength, but this leads to a controversial conclusion,” indicates Gilbert. “The best nutritional intervention to increase muscle and strength is eating a high-protein diet. However, many scientists argue that high-protein diets have the opposite effect on longevity. So, if we can’t even agree on that, you can see that science has a long way to go to try and figure this out.”.

Industry observers note that one stat Hosmer found particularly striking was that over 70 percent of the biological pathways affected were the same across all ten diets. “I interpret that to mean that no single superfood is doing the work, and it affirms that [a combination of] food, diet, and nutrition impacts us on the cellular level. The foods these patterns share are what matter,” says Hosmer, who, along with Gilbert, breaks down the standouts:.

It has been revealed that alongside individual foods, Hosmer indicates certain diet components have the greatest impact on aging. For starters, protein is a must. “As we age, our muscles respond less efficiently to the protein we eat. This is called anabolic resistance, and in women, the drop in estrogen makes it worse,” she explains. Building and retaining muscle isn’t only about strength; Hosmer says it’s our largest site for handling blood sugar and a strong predictor of independence later in life. “Many women eat less protein just when they need more.”.

It has been revealed that gilbert adds that while protein is an important part of a balanced, longevity diet, there are some considerations to keep in mind before adding it to your meal. “I believe that because muscle and strength are so strongly associated with longevity and that protein, particularly later in life, supports them,” he indicates. The caveat, however, is that there is a potential mechanism (which has to do with the amino acid methionine) whereby too much protein could have negative effects. “Many scientists argue that, because in insects and some other animals, less protein along with calorie restriction increases lifespan, humans would similarly benefit. Also, some cite the so-called ‘Blue Zones’, alleged to show that plant-based, low-protein diets are superior. In my opinion, all of these have been shown to be invalid,” says Gilbert.

Recent findings suggest that fiber is another essential nutrient that you’ll reap from plant foods and mushrooms. Meat, fish, dairy, and eggs contain no fiber, and because our enzymes can’t break them down, Hosmer states that fiber travels intact to the large intestine to assist. Once there, fermentable fibers become food for the gut microbiome; other fibers mainly add bulk and keep things moving. “As gut bacteria ferment fiber, they make short-chain fatty acids, which nourish the cells lining the gut, help keep that barrier strong, and keep inflammation in check. Fiber also steadies blood sugar and helps the body excrete estrogen the liver has already processed, supporting healthy hormone balance. Yet more than 90 percent of American women don’t reach the recommended 21 to 25 grams a day,” Hosmer explains.

Plant diversity matters, too, and not just quantity. Hosmer points to research from the American Gut Project that found people who ate 30 or more different kinds of plant foods a week had more diverse gut microbiomes than those who ate 10 or fewer. “That’s because each plant brings its own mix of fibers and polyphenols, and some bacteria have preferences, so a varied diet feeds a broader community of microbes. A broader community does more jobs. It makes short-chain fatty acids that protect the gut lining, helps regulate immunity and inflammation, turns plant compounds into forms the body can use, and even helps process estrogen.” The variety of plants Hosmer adds seems to matter more than any single “perfect” plant.

You’ve likely heard of healthy fats, meaning omega-3s from fish and the polyphenol-rich fat in olive oil. Adding these to your diet can support cell membranes and help settle inflammation.

Sources indicate that also on the list for Gilbert is vitamin D, which he states studies have shown to be inversely related to the risk of mortality. “This does not prove that low vitamin D is the cause, but it is compelling evidence. Although some results are controversial, low [vitamin D] levels have been linked to all-cause, cardiovascular, cancer, and infection-related mortality,” he adds. Vitamin D is intimately involved in immunity, too. It protects T-cell immune response.

Although Gilbert says, “The only thing all good nutritionists agree on is that there is no one ‘best’ diet or ‘best’ food,” he warns that for most people, minimizing the intake of sugar and refined, starchy grains and increasing protein intake is, in my opinion and experience, the best approach, but, again, different people can thrive on different diets. “As in the examples I gave, many of these foods contain phytochemicals—plant chemicals like polyphenols, flavanols, cyanidins, and others – which affect disease risk or support systems in the body that are likely to serve you well in old age.”.

Hosmer notes several other red flags as contributing to unhealthy skin: Diets dominated by refined carbohydrates and added sugars, heavily processed meat, and regular alcohol. “Each of these drives the chronic, low-grade inflammation researchers call “inflammaging,” and blood-sugar instability.”.

It has been revealed that having seen so many gaps in these crucial nutrients in her practice, and understanding how women’s bodies change in midlife, led Hosmer and her team to build Menomix at MenoPantry. “One serving adds meaningful protein along with ground flaxseed and psyllium fiber, plus a range of plant ingredients. It’s made to help close the protein, fiber, and plant-variety gaps that so many women are carrying,” she adds.

To dive deeper into some of those gaps or bad habits that can send skin aging off the rails, Hosmer offers some eating patterns that push biology in the wrong direction:.

In a recent development, the information can be overwhelming, but instead of purging everything in your fridge, Hosmer suggests first focusing on adding good foods instead of restricting less healthful options. “In my experience, that’s more sustainable, both because it feels less like deprivation and because the “good” foods can displace the ones that speed aging up instead of slowing it down. You don’t need to pick the “right” diet and follow it perfectly.”.

She highlights that the DZNE study found few people scored well on all ten diets at once, yet better adherence to any of them helped. What matters is the common ground. Mediterranean, Nordic, DASH, MIND, and plant-based diets vary on the plate, but they have a common core: more fruits, vegetables, and whole grains, and less red and processed meat, and added sugar. “That shared core is where I’d start,” notes Hosmer, offering this meal planning guide:.

Industry observers note that increase your familiarity with, and use of, plant-based proteins. Plant-based proteins offer an excellent package of beneficial nutrients, including fiber (not found in animal products). If you aren’t already familiar, learn how to include whole soy foods (tofu, tempeh, edamame) in your diet; add beans and peas and lentils to dishes here and there. Nuts and seeds and nut and seed butters count here also.

Build meals around vegetables and fruit. Fill half your plate with them, and choose deep colors like leafy greens, berries, beets, and cabbage-family vegetables. Those colors come from polyphenols, plant compounds that act as antioxidants and feed beneficial gut bacteria.

Make your grains whole and varied. Oats, rye, barley, brown rice, and whole-wheat bread are staples of the Nordic and DASH patterns, the two most consistently linked to slower aging in this study. Try a grain you haven’t eaten before—quinoa? Farro? Millet or teff? They are all cooked the same way—in boiling water, just with different grain-to-water ratios. Note: raise fiber gradually, with plenty of water, so your gut has time to adjust.

In a recent development, count your plants, not your calories. Aim toward 30 different kinds of plant foods a week. Veggies, fruits, nuts, seeds, whole grains, beans, peas, herbs, and spices all count. A homemade trail mix, an interesting salad, or a smoothie with a handful of fruit and veggies can add three or four at once.

Choose your fats deliberately. Most of these patterns favor unsaturated fats over saturated ones. Use extra-virgin olive oil as your everyday fat, and eat oily fish two or three times a week.

Keep red and processed meat occasional, and keep added sugar low. Every one of these diets limits them.

Quality matters. Note that “plant-based” isn’t automatically healthy. A version of the plant-based diet built on refined grains, sweets, and sugary drinks tended to be associated with faster aging, as did a pro-inflammatory eating pattern overall. Food quality matters, not just food category.

According to recent reports, diet is the foundation the other efforts rest on. Collagen supplements and skin care can help, but they can’t make up for a body that lacks what it needs to build and protect tissue. According to Gilbert, collagen supplements contain very high levels of the amino acid glycine, which he notes can balance the potential harms of proteins that are high in methionine.

It has been revealed that hosmer further explains that collagen peptides break down during digestion into amino acids and small peptides. Your body then decides where to use them. “To actually build collagen, it needs enough total protein, plus vitamin C. Vitamin C is a required helper for the enzymes that stabilize the collagen structure. It also needs minerals like zinc and copper. So a collagen supplement taken on top of a protein-poor, micronutrient-poor diet is not going to be optimized,” Hosmer claims. “Collagen is also an incomplete protein: it’s low in leucine and lacks tryptophan entirely. It can add to your protein intake, but it isn’t a substitute for complete proteins when it comes to muscle.”.

Sources indicate that on the surface, what we eat affects the skin from the inside. Hosmer notes that polyphenol-rich foods and healthy fats support the skin’s own defenses against oxidative stress, and high blood sugar leads to glycation, which stiffens collagen fibers. The gut matters here, too. “Researchers call the connection the gut–skin axis. When the gut lining is healthy, and the microbiome is well fed, inflammation throughout the body tends to stay lower, and the skin reflects that. External products can only do so much if we aren’t supporting our skin from the inside,” Hosmer says.

In a recent development, diet plays a major role in overall skin health and slower aging, but Hosmer argues that it’s not the full picture. To optimize more youthful-looking skin, consider other factors that may be equally as key as diet.

In a recent development, they say that nature is cyclical, and it’s true that there comes a time every year when the celebrities flock to Aspen, Colorado, to enjoy the colder seasons on the slopes and in chalets, all while showing off their luxurious winter style. And it appears that Bella Hadid is enjoying this holiday season with a upcoming friend.

Earlier this week, the supermodel and Orebella founder was spotted out and about with Nathan Lacy, a fifth-generation cowboy and the project manager at a construction tech giant in Crested Butte, Colorado, who has been seen hanging out with Hadid on a number of occasions.

On Wednesday, the two went thrift shopping arm-in-arm throughout the snowy vacation town, where each showed off their cozy mountain style.

Take a look back at her cowgirl getups or her Cannes festival gowns, and you’ll see that Hadid can switch between aesthetics with ease, and here, the chameleonic model evinced the après-ski life with a chic double-denim fit.

Up top, she wore a jean barn jacket featuring a contrasting brown corduroy collar, which she layered over a white knit, V-neck sweater, and a chocolate tee, with a gold medallion necklace stacked on top.

To complement these pops of brown, Hadid also carried a maple leather tote bag from Coach and popped on a pair of hickory-hued sunglasses.

Then, for a full Britney Spears double-denim moment, the Beauty star added a pair of straight-leg blue jeans, which rested over a set of black Doc Martens loafers. Finally, she finished off the fit with a cream beanie and gold hoop earrings.

Lacy, meanwhile, wore a khaki hoodie over a plaid henley and black jeans, which he accessorized with Converse and a Coors baseball cap. In his hand, he carried the leash of his Golden Retriever, who joined them for the shopping excursion.

Hadid and Lacy were last seen together on November 7, when they attended a Colorado Avalanches hockey game at Denver’s Ball Arena, where they sat courtside and were featured on the NHL’s official Instagram account. Days later, Hadid documented the moment on her own account as well.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, forget the traditional opening-night fanfare. If love is a many-splendored thing, apparently it’s also bright pink and best enjoyed with a ’90s dance anthem blasting in the background.

Industry observers note that william Shakespeare’s Much Ado About Nothing arrived at the Winter Garden Theatre on Thursday with an explosion of fuchsia confetti, a giant inflatable heart, and seriously impressive dance moves from Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell. Shakespeare, it seemed, was ready to party.

Following its successful run in London’s West End, the production crossed the Atlantic with Hiddleston and Atwell reprising their roles as Benedick and Beatrice, two sharp-witted characters who trade barbs before falling in love. At the show’s helm is acclaimed British director Jamie Lloyd, known for his bold, contemporary reimaginings of classic plays and musicals. With Much Ado About Nothing, he’s given Shakespeare’s romantic comedy a gloriously over-the-top makeover.

Sources indicate that the party started long before the curtain rose. From the moment guests stepped into the Winter Garden, ushers danced down the aisles, greeting theatergoers as though they were arriving at the hottest club. Cynthia Nixon, Rachel Zegler, Bryan Cranston, Claire Danes, Angela Bassett, Bob Odenkirk, Hugh Dancy, and Busy Philipps were among the familiar faces in the crowd, which had enough star power to rival the theatrical fireworks unfolding onstage.

In a recent development, as Benedick and Beatrice, Hiddleston, best known to many as Marvel’s Loki, and Atwell, who played Agent Peggy Carter in the MCU, made an irresistibly mischievous pairing—dancing, singing, and flirting with infectious enthusiasm. Their characters’ courtship is one of literature’s great enemies-to-lovers stories, and the pair brought every barb, raised eyebrow, and moment of romantic tension brilliantly to life.

“I can’t do much, but I can lunge,” Hiddleston modestly told Vogue of his dancing before curtain. “The dancing is sufficiently irreverent and giddy and silly and free as this play, and I’m having the best time.”.

It has been revealed that dressed in a Ralph Lauren tuxedo, he described his opening-night feelings as “joyous and joyful,” declaring his love for the play, his fellow cast members, and the production. It was during his previous collaboration with Lloyd that the seeds for this one were planted. “When I was last on Broadway, for the production of Betrayal, Jamie mentioned to me on the last night, ‘What are we doing next?’ I thought he was joking and I said, ‘Much Ado About Nothing,’ and here we are!”.

For Atwell, the evening marked a major milestone in her nearly 25-year acting career: she was making her Broadway debut. Clad in a chic Erdem ensemble, she reflected on the significance of the occasion shortly before taking the stage. “It’s really remarkable. It’s not lost on me how special this moment is,” she said. “Rather than being overwhelmed by it, I really want to take it in and to cherish it.” She described herself as staying “calm amongst the excitable storm of it all.”.

Atwell was also having a blast with the production’s choreography, giving audiences a chance to see a different side of her. “I don’t have any formal dance training apart from going to the clubs,” she stated, laughing. “I get to have a party every night onstage, and make moves I didn’t know I had. So it’s really fun.” The dancing came with a few occupational hazards, however, including sore knees and the occasional spill. “I’ve already slipped on my ass twice, and that felt like an initiation,” she shared. Rather than rattling her, the falls actually made her more confident: “I can survive this. I can get up and carry on.”.

Sources indicate that for all the fuchsia and dance-floor theatrics, the production left the Bard’s text alone. “I’ve always believed that Shakespeare should be spoken as if it was written right now or yesterday,” Hiddleston said. “There’s no word of this play that isn’t the 400-year-old text by Shakespeare. We have dressed it in the energy of dancing and music and levity, but the play itself is the play that it always was.”.

Industry observers note that he went on: “Come because it will speak to your heart. This play is funny. It’s been funny for 400 years. We’ll make it easy for you.”.

Dressed in a custom pink Levi’s suit, Lloyd told Vogue that the show’s abundance of confetti—which erupts during a jubilant party scene, blanketing the stage and eventually spilling into the audience—is about more than just spectacle. “It’s certainly a lot and it’s used in a really exciting way, to show the celebration of love and joy—and that’s what the play is all about. It feels like we really need that right now.”.

The party continued well after the curtain came down. Following a standing ovation, the cast and guests headed to Tavern on the Green for the after-party, where lavish food stations served tacos, pasta, salmon, and steak skewers, while the Prosecco flowed—and, yes, people hit the dance floor.

How to Care for a Thanksgiving Cactus so It Blooms Right on Time
